Although short-term yield forecasting has advanced, long-term early warning frameworks remain scarce. Moreover, reliance on post-harvest yield statistics and static zonation in YG analysis limits the spatiotemporal sensitivity required for forward-looking agricultural management and for alleviating food supply pressures. To address these challenges, we propose the YS-RYG-IMF framework, which integrates six-month-ahead yield prediction with dynamic YG identification to establish a closed-loop pathway from early evaluation to differentiated intervention. The framework comprises three modules: (1) rice yield prediction six months before maturity using the BC-HRF model, which incorporates climate, soil, vegetation, and topographic variables and mitigates regression-to-the-mean effects; (2) dynamic identification of the annual attainable yield (Ya, 95th percentile) through ISODATA clustering, while YG dynamics are quantified through a moving-window linear regression (MWLR) approach; and (3) classification of YG trend into “steady growth”, “ceiling pressure”, and “stalled floor” types via a three-element typology, followed by construction of a regional priority map for yield improvement. Applied to the Yangtze River Delta (2006–2021), the results showed that the BC-HRF model achieved effective early yield forecasting (R 2 =0.65, RMSE=700 kg ha −1 ), although uncertainties remained under extreme climatic conditions. Overall, regional rice yields increased steadily, while northern Jiangsu and northern Anhui exhibited slowing or declining trends. The “ceiling pressure” and “stalled floor” types showed increasing north–south spatial heterogeneity, suggesting that yield improvement potential is more constrained in southern regions. Priority zoning analysis indicated that 71.4% of Jiangsu was classified as first-priority areas, compared with 17.9% in Zhejiang and 10.9% in Shanghai, revealing pronounced interregional disparities in yield potential and management requirements. Further OLS regression results demonstrated that climate conditions, cultivation systems, and socioeconomic factors exerted differentiated driving effects across provinces. In summary, the YS-RYG-IMF framework links prediction, classification, and zoning to provide both a theoretical foundation and methodological support for early warning and differentiated management of agricultural systems under climate change, with transferability and policy relevance.

title: Spatiotemporal coupling assessment of human–nature relationships in ecologically sensitive areas under intensive anthropogenic activities
abstract: Quantifying the directional interactions between ecological quality and anthropogenic intensity is crucial for sustainable development. However, the nonlinear response characteristics and threshold effects of human–nature systems remain inadequately explored. This study conducted a spatiotemporal coupling assessment of human–nature relationships in the Henan section of the Yellow River Basin from 2000 to 2020 within the “Pattern–Interaction–Mechanism–Threshold” framework. Ecological quality was represented by the Remote Sensing Ecological Index (RSEI) constructed from MODIS data, while human activity intensity was quantified using Human Footprint (HF) data. The coupling coordination degree model was adopted to evaluate human–nature interactions, and the Geodetector model was employed to reveal the key driving factors. Furthermore, the constraint line and the piecewise linear regression methods were applied to identify ecological response thresholds. The results indicated that the RSEI decreased from 2000 to 2020, reaching its lowest point in 2015. Despite a significant negative spatial correlation between the RSEI and HF, both increased concurrently during 2000–2010 and 2015–2020. Over 58 % of the basin exhibited imbalanced coupling, with human-dominated areas expanding. Distance to major roads and temperature were the key drivers influencing the coupling level, with the explanatory power consistently above 0.25. The ecological response threshold followed a “rise–decline–rebound” trend and is projected to reach 32.7 by 2030, exceeding the 2010 peak. Special attention should be directed to HF Level III regions (30 ≤ HF < 40) in the central and northern parts to prevent degradation risks from sustained disturbances. These findings provide a scientific basis for the ecological management of sensitive regions.

title: Coupling dynamics of human-environment systems in the large lake basin: Spatiotemporal interactions and driving mechanisms of ecosystem services and human footprint intensity
abstract: High-intensity human activities are reshaping the pattern of ecosystem services (ESs) and threatening the sustainability of human–environment systems (HES) in large lake basins. To elucidate the coupling mechanisms of such systems, this study constructs a model based on ESs and human footprint intensity (HFI). First, the Sen-MK trend and center-of-gravity migration models are used to characterize the spatiotemporal dynamics of the system. Next, exploratory spatial data analysis (ESDA) is combined with the coupling coordination degree (CCD) model to examine the spatial dependence structure and the coupled evolution patterns of the HES. Finally, the XGBoost-SHAP machine learning framework is applied to reveal the nonlinear interaction mechanisms among key driving factors. Using the Dongting Lake Basin as a case study, the results show the following. First, between 2000 and 2020, ESs and HFI exhibited significant spatial mismatches. The total ESs initially declined and then rebounded to 33 %, concentrating in upstream areas. In contrast, high HFI zones expanded from 13 % to 25 %, continuously clustering in downstream urban regions. Second, the HES exhibited a typical “contraction in the middle, expansion at both ends” pattern. Medium-coordination zones decreased by 10.9 %, while low-coordination zones increased by 135 %. Upstream ecological barrier areas and downstream urban clusters remained relatively stable, whereas the coordination in midstream transitional zones significantly deteriorated. Third, carbon storage, NDVI, and water yield constitute the ecological gain system of ESs, while population and GDP form the development pressure system. Significant synergistic enhancement exists among ecological elements, amplifying their positive effects on system coupling. Overall, the sustainable development of HES requires a comprehensive basin assessment and a systems coupling perspective. This study provides a scientific basis for hierarchical governance in large lake basins.

title: Assessment of optical vegetation indices for characterization of mangrove phenology
abstract: • Evaluated the performance of 26 vegetation indices from 6 categories for mangrove phenology. • Proposed the novel methods of time series reconstruction and VI assessment. • The chlorophyll- and water content-related VIs performed the best. • The structure-related VIs showed moderate performance. • The mangrove phenological patterns of different vegetation indices exhibited asynchrony. Mangroves are coastal ecosystems with salt-tolerant, evergreen trees and shrubs. Investigating mangrove phenology is significant for understanding their seasonal dynamics and ecological processes. To date, Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) have been commonly used to monitor mangrove phenology from satellites, while other vegetation indices capturing physiological and biochemical characteristics of plants are rarely applied. With Sentinel-2 satellite imagery from 2019 to 2022 covering mangrove forests in China, we evaluated the performance of various optical vegetation indices from six classes related to structure, chlorophylls, carotenoids and anthocyanins, water content, dry matter, and photosynthesis, for mangrove phenology characterization, and compared the phenological patterns exhibited by them. We firstly selected 26 vegetation indices and improved the Harmonic ANalysis of Time Series (HANTS) algorithm for time series reconstruction. Then, we developed the Reconstruction Quality Index (RQI) and the Normalized Cumulative Reconstruction Success Rate (RSR nc ) to evaluate the capability of all vegetation indices in mangrove phenology characterization. Based on RSR nc , the five top-performing vegetation indices of different classes, including MERIS Terrestrial Chlorophyll Index (MTCI), Normalized Difference Infrared Index (NDII), Normalized Burnt Ratio (NBR), EVI and Near-Infrared Reflectance of vegetation (NIRv), were further employed for the extraction of phenometrics. Finally, the satellite-observed phenological patterns were intercompared with litter data. The results show that (1) chlorophyll- and water content-related vegetation indices outperformed the commonly used structure-related in characterizing seasonal patterns of mangroves, with EVI and NIRv showing earlier phenological patterns than MTCI, NDII, and NBR by 30–50 days. (2) An RQI-based model selection strategy enhanced reconstruction quality, while RSR nc effectively assessed the phenological characterization ability of different vegetation indices. (3) All VIs were negatively correlated with litter, with MTCI, NDII, and NBR achieving stronger correlations at shorter time lags than EVI and NIRv.

title: Operationalizing SDGs through the Water-Energy-Food Nexus: multi-level assessment of ecosystem service supply-demand patterns in China
abstract: • Integrated Water-Energy-Food nexus reveals ecosystem service supply demand dynamics in China. • Revealed scale‑dependent Water-Energy-Food linkages and distinct regional patterns across multiple administrative levels. • Proposed a scheme structured around zonal control, classified strategy, and hierarchical management to achieve the SDGs. Global climate change and human society's development have escalated the imbalance between the supply and demand of Ecosystem services (ESs). Clarifying the relationship between the supply and demand of ecosystem service and elucidating its multi-scaled spatiotemporal evolution offers vital comprehensive supporting information for sustainable development. This study integrates the interactions between human-activities, natural-ecosystems, and socio-economics from a water-energy-food nexus perspective, covering multiple sustainable development dimensions, including SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), and SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities). The ESs from a water-energy-food nexus perspective were quantified by the water yield, carbon sequestration, and food production. The relationship among the supply–demand balance for water yield, carbon sequestration, and food production was analysed by the supply–demand index. We also investigated the spatial scale effects of each ecosystem service across various administrative levels (provincial, municipal, and county). The results shown that: (1) From 2000 to 2020, the supply of China's ESs in water-energy-food nexus exceeded demand overall, with limited spatial heterogeneity yet pronounced internal disparities. (2) The individual supply–demand ratio of China's ESs in water-energy-food nexus has shown a gradual improvement trend with notable spatial heterogeneity (2000–2020), but decline in carbon storage, and the integrated supply–demand ratio for the water-energy-food nexus fluctuates upwards. (3) Water-energy-food exhibit different interrelationships at various spatial scales, demonstrating regional characteristics. Furthermore, we proposed an integrated water-energy-food management scheme and policy recommendations in the principles of “zonal control, classified strategy, and hierarchical management”. Our study systematically incorporates ecosystem service supply–demand dynamics and their interdependencies into ecological conservation and restoration planning, providing innovative approaches for achieving sustainable human-environment system co-development and circular resource management.

title: Spatio-temporal variations in global ecosystem respiration and its drivers over the last two decades
abstract: Ecosystem respiration (ER) is a fundamental component of the global carbon cycle, and its accurate estimation is essential for understanding global carbon budgets and climate change. In recent years, machine learning algorithms have been increasingly employed for ER estimation; however, existing ER data products derived from such methods exhibit considerable uncertainties in temporal dynamics. In this study, we reconstructed the time series of ER using eddy covariance flux observations and corresponding driver data, developed annual ER prediction models, and produced a global ER dataset (RCS_ER) at 0.05° spatial resolution for the period 2000–2020. Comparative analyses show that our product consistently outperforms existing global ER datasets in terms of annual and overall simulation accuracy. While the spatial distribution of RCS_ER is highly consistent with previous products, it reveals stronger interannual variability and an overall increasing trend over the past two decades, with significant spatial heterogeneity in trend patterns. Partial correlation analysis further indicated that carbon substrates is the dominant driver of ER interannual variability (IAV) in most global regions, while precipitation exerts a more substantial influence than temperature in modulating regional ER dynamics. These findings provide an important data foundation for studying the spatio-temporal variations of terrestrial carbon fluxes and improve our understanding of global carbon cycle processes.

title: Towards rebuilding algae communities in post-mining ditches
abstract: Algae, as organisms known to occur in extreme environments and accumulate pollutants, can be effective in purifying post-mining waters. Algal flora, for the first time sampled from two post-mining ditches in the area of Upper Silesia (Southern Poland), is characterized by low biodiversity. In this study, we examined the possibility of using mainly autochthonous (indigenous) diatoms and green algal strains from these two ditches, but also some allochthonous green and xanthophyte algal strains from a sewage treatment plant, as so-called biological starters. The use of biological starters, i.e. algal mats growing on solid substrate, prepared in laboratory conditions for placement in post-mining waters, is a new method developed to increase their biodiversity and accelerate purification processes. The rate of biological mass increase for individual algal strains, both one-celled and filamentous, growing together on solid substrate as examined in the water collected from the two ditches under experimental laboratory conditions. Several autochtonous one-celled diatoms, especially Pinnularia appendiculata, and filamentous green algae, Klebsormidium sp. and Mougeotia sp., as well as one allochtonous one-celled green alga, Tetradesmus lagerheimii, turned out to be the most resistant to the conditions prevailing in both ditches, and at the same time the most suitable for inhabiting this type of habitats. These algal taxa were the most important element in the structure of biological starters on solid substrates. Next, the potential of the biological starters to bioaccumulate chemical compounds occurring in elevated concentrations in degraded mine watercourses should be investigated.

title: Effect of acid production from forest litter on available heavy metals in soil of surrounding farmland
abstract: • Forest litter leaching reduced soil pH and increased exchangeable Al 3+ . • Leaching increased soil heavy metal availability by up to 5.48-fold. • Longer leaching and stronger acidity increased heavy metal availability. • Mantel test revealed strong links between acidity, soil properties, and metal levels. • Forest litter decomposition acidifies soil and enhances heavy metal availability. Litter decomposition is a central ecological process in forests because of its role in nutrient cycling and the maintenance of soil fertility. Products of litter decomposition affect the physicochemical properties of soil and the activity of mineral elements. However, the effects of these decomposition products on soil properties and heavy metal availability in surrounding farmland remain poorly understood. In this study, we examined three types of typical forest litter— Myrica rubra leaves, Bambusa cerosissima leaves, and Pinus sylvestris leaves—collected from Daluo Mountain, Wenzhou, China, to investigate their effects on soil chemical properties and heavy metal availability in adjacent farmland. Litter decomposition and leaching experiments showed that leachate exposure caused soil acidification, with pH decreasing by up to 0.15 units, while the maximum level of exchangeable Al 3+ (Ex-Al 3+ ) increased by 133 %. At the same time, the availability of heavy metals such as Cr, Mn, Ni, Cu, Zn, As, Cd, and Pb rose by up to 5.48-fold. Higher levels of low-molecular-weight organic acids and longer leaching durations intensified heavy metal availability, especially in the 0–20 cm and 20–40 cm soil layers. The Mantel test revealed significant correlations ( p < 0.001) between soil acidity, chemical properties, and available heavy metals, particularly Mn, Ni, Cu, Zn, As, and Cd. Partial least squares path modeling (PLS-PM) showed that forest litter decomposition led to soil acidification, which further affected available heavy metals ( p < 0.001). With an estimated 65 % decomposition rate, annual forest litter in Daluo Mountain was calculated to contribute approximately 3.6 × 10 3 mol of H + , highlighting its role in altering soil chemistry and increasing heavy metal risks in adjacent farmland. These findings provide a theoretical foundation for assessing and controlling heavy metals in farmland and contribute to the sustainable management of farmland ecosystems.

title: How does environmental governance influence terrestrial ecosystem service values? A case study based on the SD-PLUS model
abstract: • SD-PLUS model simulates how policies shape future land-use and ecosystem services. • Ecological protection policies can shrink ecosystem service cold spots by 2030. • Converting cropland to forest enhances the spatial flow of ecosystem services. • A transferable framework reveals how governance boosts ecosystem services. Evaluating ecosystem service value (ESV) plays a crucial role in supporting decision-making, which land −use is one of the key drivers in ESV. However, the influence of policy factors on land-use changes is often overlooked or oversimplified in ESV assessments. In this study, taking Nanping City as a case, we incorporated policy factors related to environmental governance into the Ecological Protection Scenario (EPS), and established the Conventional Development Scenario (CDS) and the Economic Development Scenario (EDS) as controls to evaluate the impact of environmental governance on ESV with System Dynamics (SD)–Patch-generating Land-Use Simulation (PLUS) model. The hot spot analysis was conducted subsequently. The results indicated that the ESVs in CDS, EDS and EPS were 217.317, 219.732 and 220.522 billion yuan in 2030, and the changes from 2020 were −1.43%, −0.34% and 0.02%, respectively. The conversion of forestland into cropland dominated in CDS, whereas the conversion of cropland into forestland dominated in EPS. In EPS, the area of ESV cold spots decreased the most relative to 2020. These findings underscore the need for governance strategies that move beyond traditional area-based conservation. We propose spatially tiered ecological markets, industry-ecology integration, and ESV-weighted performance audits to better align policies with regional ecological capacities. Rather than focusing solely on the magnitude of ESV gains, this study highlights the importance of spatial functionality and institutional coherence, offering new perspectives for socioecological modernization in land-use planning.

title: Performance of Trophic State Index in eutrophication assessment in Chinese lakes: Regional-specific drivers and management implications
abstract: • Conventional Trophic State Index (TSI) misrepresents algal bloom risks in Chinese lakes. • Regional climate and morphometry strongly affect TSI, showing poor general applicability. • Ecoregion-adaptive recalibration is needed to improve the accuracy of eutrophication management. The Trophic State Index (TSI), based on chlorophyll- a [TSI(Chl a )], Secchi depth [TSI(SD)], total nitrogen [TSI(TN)], and total phosphorus [TSI(TP)], is widely used to assess lake eutrophication. However, its application across ecologically diverse regions assumes consistent nutrient–Chl a –SD relationships—an assumption often violated in heterogeneous regions like China. Using data from 242 lakes across five major ecoregions in China, we evaluated the accuracy of TSI(TN), TSI(TP), and TSI(SD) as proxies for TSI(Chl a ). Significant discrepancies emerged, with national mean absolute percentage errors (MAPEs) of 62.3% for TSI(TN) and 68.5% for TSI(TP). The Tibetan Plateau Lake Region showed the largest errors (142.5% for TSI(TN) and 151.9% for TSI(TP)), primarily due to cold-climate suppression of algal nutrient assimilation. The Inner Mongolian-Xinjiang (33.9%, 23.7%) and Northeast Mountain and Plain (43.7%, 49.1%) Lake Regions also exhibited elevated MAPEs, mainly driven by low temperatures. In contrast, the Eastern Plain Lake Region showed lower MAPEs for TSI(TN) and TSI(TP) (16.1%, 19.9%), as did the Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau Lake Region (20.9%, 31.4%), due to favorable thermal and light conditions. Notably, TSI(TN) underestimated bloom risks in the Eastern Plain Lake Region due to high nitrogen use efficiency. TSI(SD) showed a national MAPE of 47.3% and tended to overestimate bloom risks, with regional MAPEs ranging from 18.9% to 92.7%, mainly due to non-algal turbidity—such as sediment resuspension and chromophoric dissolved organic matter—that interferes with the transparency–algal biomass relationship. We recommend region-specific recalibration of TSI sub-indices and tailored bloom control strategies based on algal sensitivity to nutrient and light attenuation. This study highlights the limitations of uniform TSI frameworks and supports adaptive eutrophication management.

title: Revealing two decades of water quality dynamics and driving mechanism in the Qinjiang river using multi-source data and LSTM-eKAN model
abstract: • CE-MSI-ED achieved robust water extraction (OA:0.96–0.99) across Qinjiang River sections/seasons (2003–2023). • Water body area/width exhibited a nonlinear decline after initial growth, peaking in summer. • LSTM-eKAN outperformed CNN-LSTM in time-series water quality inversion. • Water quality improved significantly, particularly downstream, while remaining optimal in midstream. • Hydrological and anthropogenic drivers dominated the spatio-temporal variations of water quality. Understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of water body morphology and quality, including their driving mechanisms, is crucial for effective water resource management, ecological conservation, and sustainable development. However, the inherent complexity of these systems hinders understanding of their change mechanisms. This study proposed a novel water extraction method, the Collaborative Enhancement of Multi-Spectral Indices and Elevation Data (CE-MSI-ED), which achieved accurate delineation (Overall Accuracy ranging from 0.96 to 0.99) of seasonal water bodies throughout the upstream, midstream, and downstream of the Qinjiang River from 2003 to 2023. Analysis revealed a nonlinear temporal trend in water area and width, characterized by initial increases followed by declines, which varied spatially across river sections and seasonally over the two decades. We developed an innovative Long Short-Term Memory − enhanced Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (LSTM-eKAN) for water quality (WQ) inversion by integrating measured data and optimized multispectral features. Compared to the conventional Convolutional Neural Network − Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM), LSTM-eKAN demonstrated outstanding performance (R 2 = 0.52–0.85) in time-series inversion of Dissolved Oxygen (DO), Ammonia Nitrogen (NH 3 -N), and Permanganate Index (COD Mn ) across the entire river, achieving an average R 2 improvement of 0.13. Significant WQ improvements occurred basin-wide: DO increased by 0.32–1.03 mg/L, while NH 3 -N and COD Mn decreased by 0.01–1.28 mg/L and 0.04–1.01 mg/L, respectively. Mantel tests and Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) identified key drivers of WQ variation. Synergistic effects of human activities (path coefficient = 0.54, p < 0.001), meteorological, and hydrological factors (path coefficient = 0.70, p < 0.001) collectively governed WQ dynamics. Gross Domestic Product (GDP), runoff, and water temperature exhibited particularly significant effects on WQ. Meteorological variables indirectly negatively influenced WQ by regulating hydrological processes, with precipitation demonstrating a more pronounced impact than air temperature. These findings provide valuable scientific support for large-scale, long-term coastal river WQ monitoring and informed aquatic ecosystem management.

title: Optimizing remote sensing methods for forest stand density estimation in mountainous areas: a UAV-sentinel-2 synergy
abstract: Stand density is a key parameter for assessing forest structure and ecological function, and its remote sensing-based estimation is critically important for monitoring forest carbon stocks. As the primary component of forest resources in southern China, plantations are typically distributed across mountainous regions with complex terrain. The estimation of stand density using remote sensing in these areas faces numerous challenges due to factors such as topographic variation and interference from understory vegetation. Taking Shaoguan City in Guangdong Province as a case study, this research focuses on typical plantation areas dominated by Eucalyptus , Cunninghamia lanceolata , and Pinus massoniana , and proposes an optimized estimation method that integrates multi-source remote sensing data. Several improvements were made upon traditional approaches, including: (1) the Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI) was utilized to reduce interference from understory vegetation and improve the accuracy of canopy cover estimation for standing trees; (2) the Modified Green-Red Vegetation Index (MGRVI) was introduced to improve the accuracy of individual tree canopy cover estimation; (3) the SCS+C topographic correction method was employed to mitigate the effects of terrain factors-specifically slope and aspect-on the accuracy of surface reflectance derived from remote sensing data; (4) a comparative experiment across spatial resolutions of 10 m, 30 m, 60 m, and 90 m was conducted, and 30 m was identified as the optimal scale for stand density estimation, offering a balance between accuracy and regional adaptability. The study demonstrates that tree species classification using the Random Forest algorithm achieved an accuracy of 93.22 %. Stand density estimation attained the highest performance at a 30 m × 30 m spatial resolution, with an R 2 of 0.85 and an RMSE of fewer than 40 trees per hectare. These results highlight the effectiveness of the proposed method for accurately and efficiently estimating stand density in mountainous plantation forests, offering practical support for regional forest resource inventories and ecological assessments.

title: Indirect effects of temperature driven seasonal succession of phytoplankton communities in a tropical reservoir
abstract: • Indirect effects of temperature driven phytoplankton succession in the tropical reservoir. • The indirect effects depended on mixing regime associated with nutrient availability. • The driving role of temperature strengthens as water stability and depth increase spatially. • The driving role of temperature varies as inter-annual nutrient levels changing. Understanding the driving role of temperature on phytoplankton succession is of fundamental importance to predict the effects of climate change on freshwater ecosystem structure and function. This role encompasses both a direct constraint on algal growth and indirect environmental modification through regulation of mixing regime. To identify the importance of direct and indirect effects of temperature on phytoplankton seasonal succession in tropical reservoirs, we conducted a dry-season investigation along a longitudinal gradient and a 10-year annual investigation of a lacustrine habitat in a large tropical reservoir in southern China. The study confirmed the spatial–temporal heterogeneity of temperature as a driving effect on phytoplankton seasonal succession. The spatial comparison helped identify the importance of indirect environmental regulation of temperature for phytoplankton seasonal succession in the tropical reservoir. A cooling-driven mixing process led to changes in the nutrient supply regime, from depletion of both nitrogen and phosphorus to depletion of only phosphorus coinciding with turnover of cyanobacteria to diatoms in lacustrine habitats. This process was constrained in turbulent riverine environments. Owing to the valid temperature constraint, resources-availability-driven cyanobacterial dominance occurred in all seasons during the 10-year annual investigation in the lacustrine habitat. Our results suggest that focusing on variations in resource availability along temperature-driven mixing processes can improve predictions of phytoplankton community structure response to temperature change in tropical reservoirs.

title: Responses and shifting drivers of ecosystem carbon fluxes under drought conditions
abstract: • Ecosystems are most sensitive to short-term droughts (1–3 months). • NEP exhibits a nonlinear threshold response, declining sharply when SPEI-6 < -1.5. • Drought shifts NEP limiting factors from energy availability to water supply. Net ecosystem productivity (NEP), i.e., the balance between carbon uptake and respiration, is a critical indicator of ecosystem carbon dynamics under climate extremes. The effects of drought on ecosystem carbon fluxes were investigated via eddy covariance observations from 77 flux sites worldwide (FLUXNET2015, ChinaFLUX, and the Heihe network), with drought quantified on the basis of the standardized precipitation evapotranspiration index (SPEI) across multiple timescales ranging from 1–12 months (SPEI-1 to SPEI-12). The results revealed that ecosystems were most sensitive to short-term drought (1–3 months), with most sites exhibiting maximum carbon flux–SPEI correlations. Although short-term moisture variability drove immediate responses in carbon fluxes, the cumulative moisture stress over seasonal timescales (SPEI-6) indicated a significant threshold response in these fluxes: relative to normal conditions (SPEI-6 > − 0.5), the NEP increased slightly under mild to moderate drought conditions (−1.5 < SPEI-6 ≤ − 0.5). However, for SPEI-6 ≤ − 1.5 (severe drought), the NEP decreased sharply, indicating that adaptive mechanisms were compromised beyond the critical SPEI-6 threshold of − 1.5. Notably, wetlands (WET) and mixed forests (MF) maintained their carbon-sink functions even under severe drought, indicating substantial drought resistance through hydrological buffering and functional diversity. Moreover, the results of SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis revealed that the leaf area index (LAI) was the main regulator of the NEP, contributing approximately 30 % under both nondrought and drought conditions. Relative to normal conditions, drought modulated the controls on carbon fluxes: the importance of canopy conductance (Gc) increased from 17.93 % to 25.52 % (+7.59 percentage points), whereas the importance of net radiation (Rn) decreased from 19.81 % to 9.09 % (−10.72 percentage points), indicating a transition from energy to water limitation in terms of ecosystem carbon dynamics. These findings establish a critical seasonal drought threshold for ecosystem carbon dynamics and capture the shift from energy to water limitation in carbon flux regulation, offering actionable insights for ecosystem management and drought resilience strategies.

title: Integrating the AE-AM model and the SMI-P framework for water environmental security assessment: A case study of the Chushandian Reservoir basin
abstract: • Developed an AE-AM model within the SMI-P framework to assess water environmental security at a refined raster-scale. • Identified SPEI and RUSLE as the dominant drivers, with TWS, WC, WY, and SSM as secondary contributors. • Revealed the dynamic impacts of climate changes, soil erosion, and human activities on water environment security. • Applied SHAP and obstacle analysis to disentangle positive/negative contributions of indicators. • Verified model robustness and reliability through Monte Carlo simulation, expert scoring, and field validation. Water environmental security issues have become prominent with the rapid development of the economy and society. Scientifically conducting assessments is of great significance for identifying potential risks, protecting water resources, and promoting regional collaborative development. Integrating the AE-AM model and SMI-P framework, this study proposes a refined raster-scale water environmental security assessment for the case study of Chushandian Reservoir Basin from 2016 to 2023. The objectives are to identify key indicators, reveal spatiotemporal dynamics, and provide scientific support for watershed management. The results indicate that (1) SPEI and RUSLE are the dominant driving factors of water environmental security, while TWS, WC, WY, and SSM play secondary roles; (2) spatiotemporal analysis reveals a drought-wet-drought change pattern between 2016 and 2023, with relatively high security in water bodies and mountainous vegetation zones, but lower security in urbanized and intensively cultivated regions; (3) obstacle degree reveals the highest constrained factors are SPEI and RUSLE, while SHAP contribution further confirms the negative impacts (RUSLE and WC) and positive impacts (TWS, SPEI, WY, and SSM); (4) uncertainty and perturbation sensitivity analysis indicate data-layer and model-layer uncertainties are generally within acceptable ranges, and weight consistency with expert judgment demonstrates the robustness of the proposed methods. Overall, this study provides a dynamic and refined raster scale method for assessing water environmental security and offers valuable implications for adaptive management and basin governance.

title: Temporal–spatial characteristics of carbon emissions and low-carbon efficiency of regional energy consumption: A case study of Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, Yangtze River Delta and Sichuan-Chongqing regions
abstract: Accurately identifying the key sectors of carbon emissions and the heterogeneous priorities for emission reduction constitutes an essential prerequisite for achieving low-carbon energy development. Based on the National Greenhouse Gas Emission Factor Database , This study establishes the carbon emission inventory for energy consumption in three typical regions of China from 2016 to 2023. Furthermore, by introducing strong free disposability assumption for undesirable outputs, it empirically measures the low-carbon efficiency of regional energy consumption using an improved Super-SBM-Undesirable model that incorporates the materials balance principle. The empirical results reveal the following: (1) the ranking of total carbon emissions from highest to lowest was as follows: Jiangsu, Hebei, Zhejiang, Anhui, Shanghai, Sichuan, Chongqing, Tianjin and Beijing. For the fossil energy consumption, the industrial sector constituted the primary emission source in energy terminal consumption, driven by its intensive and sustained fuel demands. The transportation sector emerged as the secondary emission source, which was attributable to the study regions’ advanced socioeconomic development and massive freight and passenger mobility needs. For the inter-regional power dispatch, Anhui and Sichuan functioned as carbon sinks, while other regions functioned as carbon sources. (2) The advantages of clean energy endowment in the Sichuan-Chongqing region created the low-carbon energy utilization advantages. The efficiency in the Yangtze River Delta region showed spatial heterogeneity. Jiangsu, Zhejiang and Shanghai fully capitalized on their strengths in regional coordinated development and intelligent transformation to advance low-carbon energy industries. In contrast, Anhui showed the lowest efficiency due to its weak foundation in low-carbon energy consumption. Beijing and Tianjin’s political status ensured stable energy supply, yet their low-carbon energy self-sufficiency remained limited. Additionally, Hebei faced with the “pollution haven” dilemma during its industrial undertaking.

title: Coupling remote sensing and hydrodynamic modeling to map submerged macrophyte restorability for large shallow lakes
abstract: Submerged-macrophyte restoration is a widely-adopted strategy to improve lake ecosystems, yet empirically determined restoration areas may not yield optimal results. To achieve a cost-effective decision, this study developed a grid-based framework to identify the highest-priority regions for submerged macrophyte restoration. The framework integrating hydrodynamic modeling (water velocity) and remote sensing data (water depth, suspended matter, photosynthetically active radiation) to calculate a Restorability Index (RI). The developed framework was applied to a large shallow lake (Lake Gehu) in eastern China during 1990-2024. The results showed that RI declined from 0.82 (1990s) to 0.46 (2020s), with a high-restorability area (RI>0.8) <1%. The RI decline can be mainly attributed to increasing suspended matter from inflow rivers and sediment resuspension. Water velocity was generally not the limited factor of low RI except the estuarine areas. Our grid-based investigation revealed that the highest-priority regions for submerged macrophyte restoration were mainly located at the south areas with high light availability (Deu≥1 m) and low flow velocity (<0.13 cm/s). Compared with previous empirical method in determining restoration regions, the framework provided a high-resolution approach to identify the highest-priority regions for submerged macrophyte restoration.

title: Patterns and drivers of aquatic biota co-occurrence networks under large-scale intensive agriculture in Northeastern China
abstract: • Land-use change (woodland-to-cropland) drives strong environmental filtering shaping species co-occurrence. • Negative correlations in co-occurrence networks reflect species segregation under filtering pressure. • Sparse and highly modular networks under strong filtering show low resilience to external disturbances. River ecosystems play an irreplaceable role in global biogeochemical cycles and the provision of ecosystem services. However, their ecological integrity is increasingly threatened by the expansion of intensive agriculture and rapid land-use transformation. Drawing on aquatic biodiversity survey data collected in the Hulan River Basin, Northeast China, between 2022 and 2025, this study constructed co-occurrence networks of phytoplankton, macroinvertebrates, and fishes to examine the impacts of land-use change on aquatic community co-occurrence patterns. The results reveal that strong environmental filtering induced by land-use change overwhelmingly shaped species co-occurrence, exerting effects far stronger than those of dispersal limitation or biotic interactions, thereby underscoring the pivotal role of human activities in restructuring community assembly mechanisms. The woodland-to-cropland conversion gradient emerged as the primary factor explaining both community composition and network modular structure, further substantiating this interpretation. The resulting sparse co-occurrence network, dominated by negative correlations, exhibited high sensitivity to the loss of key species, structural fragility, and insufficient functional redundancy to buffer against external disturbances. Overall, land-use change alters hydrological and physicochemical conditions, intensifies environmental filtering, and drives species distributions toward mutual exclusion, collectively weakening the stability and resilience of ecological networks. Management measures such as restoring riparian woodlands, restricting cropland expansion, controlling agricultural runoff, and prioritizing the conservation of key species are therefore essential to mitigate negative co-occurrence patterns, enhance network resilience, and safeguard regional biodiversity.

title: Dynamics of ecosystem service-driven networks in the Qilian Mountains and their implications for protected area management
abstract: • Assessed main ecosystem services in an ecologically fragile mountain region. • Identified key ecological patches for critical ecosystem service provision. • Found marked fluctuations in the complexity of ecosystem service networks. • Proposed targeted management strategies for priority restoration and core regulation areas. Ecosystem services-driven ecological networks are increasingly recognized as a strategic tool for guiding ecological restoration and conservation, particularly in ecologically fragile mountainous regions. However, most existing approaches remain static, often overlooking the spatiotemporal dynamics of service-driven networks in planning and management. This study proposed a framework for how to integrate multi-ecosystem services with network theory and assess network dynamics to delineate priority zones for restoration and targeted management in the Qilian Mountains. Results showed that the soil conservation, water supply, and carbon sequestration services in the study area generally improved from 2000 to 2020, and the identified key ecological patches and corridors predominantly concentrated in the eastern region. The complexity of ecosystem service-based networks fluctuated markedly over the study period, reaching its lowest point in 2010 (e.g., total corridor length dropped to 281.62 km) before partially recovering thereafter. Certain nodes (e.g., Patches 17 and 18) consistently served as the core hubs for connectivity, while others (e.g., Patches 1, 2, 8, and 24) showed high sensitivity to external disturbances. Based on these findings, targeted management recommendations were proposed for delineating priority restoration zones and core regulation areas in the Qilian Mountains protected area. This study provides a quantitative foundation for optimizing corridor restoration priorities and improving network resilience, offering methodological insights for conservation planning in arid regions globally.

title: Improving the prediction accuracy of soil organic matter: Addressing the challenge of soil moisture variability
abstract: Soil organic matter (SOM) serves as a critical indicator for assessing land degradation and plays a fundamental role in the global carbon cycle. Remote sensing-based inversion techniques provide an efficient approach to ascertain the spatial distribution of SOM at regional scales, thereby offering essential data for evaluating land degradation. However, the variability in soil moisture often interferes with the spectral reflectance captured by remote sensing imagery, which significantly limits the accuracy of SOM estimation. To address this limitation, in this study, the Google Earth Engine (GEE) cloud platform was utilized to extract bare soil pixels from over 20,000 Sentinel-2 images acquired between 2020 and 2023 according to multiple index thresholds. Three image compositing strategies were subsequently developed to reduce the influence of soil moisture, namely, the maximum bare soil composite (MaxBS), the maximum reflectance composite (MaxRef), and the minimum soil moisture composite (MinSM). These synthesized images, along with environmental covariates, were used to establish and evaluate an SOM prediction model using machine learning techniques. The results revealed that the MinSM strategy outperformed the other two methods in reducing the influence of soil moisture. Notably, the random forest model produced the most robust predictions (R2=0.73, RMSE =7.19, MAE=5.46), achieving better spatial prediction outcomes than other available open-source SOM products. Among all the variables, the annual mean temperature was identified as the most important individual predictor of SOM, whereas the spectral variables collectively contributed the most to model performance. On the basis of these results, a high-resolution spatial distribution map of SOM was generated for the Songnen black soil region, revealing a clear spatial trend of increasing SOM content from the southwest to the northeast. These findings demonstrate that the rigorous identification of bare soil pixels and the mitigation of moisture effects are critical for improving SOM mapping accuracy. This study presents a promising technical approach for achieving high-resolution SOM mapping in similar contexts to further supports the application of Nature-based Solutions (NbS) and promotes the holistic management of human-dominated landscapes.

title: Unraveling nonlinear impacts of land use change on riverine water quality under future scenarios
abstract: • A spatial modeling framework reveals LULC impacts on riverine water quality. • Nonlinear effects of landscape metrics on water quality are captured by GAMs. • The negative impacts of land-use change on water quality are stronger in low-urbanized than in highly urbanized areas. A scientific understanding of the influence of land use composition and spatial configuration on riverine water quality is essential for improving watershed environmental management. However, there is a lack of studies that capture the nonlinear, context-dependent responses of water quality to land use patterns, particularly under future socio-environmental scenarios. This study proposes a novel framework that integrates Generalized Additive Models (GAMs) and the Patch-generating Land Use Simulation (PLUS) model to predict future water quality dynamics under three SSP-RCP scenarios (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP5-8.5) from 2020 to 2050 in Jiangxi Province, China. Our findings reveal that GAMs outperform traditional linear models in capturing the intricate relationships between land use and water quality. The PLUS model proves highly compatible with the GAM framework, enabling spatially explicit simulations of future land use transitions and their effects on water quality across entire river networks. The case study highlights that hotspots of elevated nutrient concentrations, especially total nitrogen and ammonium nitrogen, are primarily located in urbanized areas with extensive impervious surfaces. Crucially, we find that the direction and magnitude of water quality changes are not dictated solely by the SSP scenario labels, but are significantly influenced by the spatial configuration, timing, and intensity of land use transitions. In particular, localized urban sprawl and intensified agriculture may exacerbate water quality degradation, even under ecologically oriented development pathways. Overall, this framework offers a transferable and spatially explicit approach to anticipating future water quality hotspots, thereby supporting proactive and informed watershed planning under conditions of uncertainty.

title: First application of multichannel GPR for root system variability analysis in Scots pine forests
abstract: Understanding the structure and variability of tree root systems is essential for assessing forest resilience under increasing climate stress. Despite their ecological significance, roots remain among the least studied components of forest ecosystems due to the limitations of traditional, invasive measurement methods. In this study, we present the first application of multichannel ground-penetrating radar (GPR) to assess the variability of root system architecture in Scots pine ( Pinus sylvestris ) stands across contrasting site conditions and developmental stand stages. Using the Stream C radar system (IDS Georadar), we conducted high-resolution 3D root mapping on 27 trees. A total of 294 roots were detected, enabling the calculation of key traits including total root number, maximum rooting depth, and average root length. Ground-truth validation through selective root excavation confirmed a high degree of correspondence between predicted and actual root positions. Root system variability was analyzed using Generalized Additive Models (GAMs), which revealed strong, non-linear effects of stand age, tree diameter (DBH), stand density (RSI), and soil type on root development. Our findings demonstrate that younger trees growing on poor, sandy soils tend to develop shallow, laterally extensive root systems, while older trees on more fertile sites exhibit deeper rooting. These preliminary patterns may offer new perspectives compared to classical excavation-based studies and highlight potential influences of both ontogeny and site characteristics on belowground structure. The successful application of multichannel GPR highlights its value as a non-invasive tool for root system assessment at ecologically meaningful scales. This approach offers new opportunities to monitor belowground responses to environmental stress and to support adaptive forest management in a changing climate.

title: Assessing combined PM2.5-O3 risks in China using a multidimensional hazard-exposure-vulnerability framework (2000–2023)
abstract: Near-surface PM 2.5 and O 3 critically impact China’s environmental and human health, yet single-pollutant risk assessments from a unidimensional perspective inadequately support macro-scale control. This study developed a multidimensional framework (hazard-exposure-vulnerability) to evaluate PM 2.5 , O 3 , and their combined risks across China from 2000 to 2023, integrating satellite-derived pollution data (CHAP), LandScan population and mortality statistics from GBD and censuses. Results reveal spatiotemporal differences among PM 2.5 and O 3 across different assessment dimensions, indicating the more comprehensive reflection of pollution risk. PM 2.5 risk peaked around 2011 before declining, while O 3 risk rose significantly post-2016. Combined risks showed a rise-decline-rise pattern with fluctuations, suggesting incomplete efficacy of coordinated controls since 2021. Areas with PM 2.5 pollution risks classified as relatively high or higher levels substantially exceeded O 3 zones during 2000–2016, but those for O 3 expanded significantly post-2017, particularly in 2019 and 2023. From 2000 to 2016, PM 2.5 and O 3 combined risks spatially coincided with PM 2.5 patterns, but after 2017, they showed superimposed effects of both pollutants. These results underscore the need for spatiotemporal stratified coordinated strategies. Macro-level governance priorities should focus on southern Xinjiang, parts of North China Plain (e.g., Tianjin, Hebei, Shandong, Henan), followed by western Tibet and Inner Mongolia, northern Gansu, southern Shanxi, eastern Hubei, and the northern Yangtze River Delta. This study enhances understanding of PM 2.5 and O 3 combined pollution dynamics and their integrated risks, providing support for coordinated pollution control and sustainable health strategies. The multidimensional assessment offers a feasible method for deconstructing the complex impacts of air pollution.

title: City layers: Vertical stratification of wild bees and the structure of urban ecological resilience
abstract: • Urban areas support diverse pollinator communities. • Bee abundance and diversity vary across vertical levels. • Bee traits influence vertical space use in urban areas. • Impervious surfaces do not exclude bees but shift their vertical distribution. • Multi-layered planning and management of greenery and nesting sites enhance pollinators. Urban environments can support diverse pollinator communities, yet their vertical stratification remains underexplored. This study examines how bee abundance, species richness, and functional diversity vary across ground, mid-story, and canopy levels in a temperate city. We sampled wild bees at three heights and assessed how ecological traits and environmental factors, including impervious surface area, green space, and tree cover, influence vertical patterns. Bee abundance and richness varied across strata, with peak abundance in the canopy and higher species richness at both ground and canopy levels. Impervious surfaces did not directly reduce overall abundance and richness, nor did they eliminate bees; instead, they appeared to alter vertical patterns with activity tending to shift upward. Vertical space use was shaped by species traits, particularly body size, nesting habits, and social strategies. Strong interactions between height and land cover further influenced species composition and functional diversity along the vertical gradient. Recognizing this vertical structuring offers new insights for biodiversity-focused city design. Our findings show that pollinator communities respond to vertical stratification, shaped by both traits and urban landscape features. This has direct implications for multi-layered greening strategies, such as tree canopy enhancement, rooftop habitats, and stratified plantings, that can improve habitat quality and ecological function in dense urban settings. The study contributes to growing evidence that vertical green infrastructure can support pollinator resilience and inform sustainable planning under intensifying land-use and climate pressures.

title: Corrigendum to “Development of island-specific land-use classification system and spatiotemporal pattern evolution analysis using Landsat time series for coastal zone management: A case study of Zhoushan Archipelago, China”. [Ecol. Indic. 179 (2025) 114158]
Corrigendum to “Soil salinization in drylands: Measure, monitor, and manage”. [Ecol. Indic. 175 (2025) 113608]
Corrigendum to “Climate sensitive growth model for volume and carbon storage of subtropical broadleaf secondary forests in China”. [Ecol. Indic. 170 (2025) 113056]
Sandy bottoms play a key role in shaping coastal fish functional β-diversity in the Mediterranean Sea
abstract: The functional diversity of temperate coastal ecosystems is strongly influenced by environmental variability and habitat characteristics. The specific contribution of different marine habitats to the functional diversity of fish communities remains comparatively understudied in temperate regions such as the Mediterranean Sea. Herein, we use a multivariate approach along with functional diversity indices to examine and compare the functional diversity and traits of fish communities in the three most abundant infralittoral Mediterranean habitats, sandy bottoms, rocky bottoms, and Posidonia oceanica meadows. The results revealed significant differences in functional diversity and traits among habitats, with variations in the ecological characteristics of fish communities. Specifically, functional traits such as the minimum depth and vertical distribution exhibited strong associations with particular habitats, influencing the functional structure of fish communities. Environmental drivers such as seabed temperature, depth, and chlorophyll concentration significantly influenced the functional composition of fish communities, as identified by partial redundancy analysis (pRDA). Among these, seabed temperature and depth explained the largest share of variation. No difference in functional redundancy was detected among habitats. Functional diversity is unevenly distributed across habitats, underscoring the significance of sandy bottoms in preserving functional beta diversity—an aspect often underrepresented in current conservation strategies. This study offers novel insights valuable for coastal biodiversity management, emphasising the complementary role of habitats in maintaining the ecological functionality of Mediterranean fish communities.

title: Drivers of remotely sensed tree height heterogeneity across spatial scales: Tree species diversity effects depend on local conditions and forest type
abstract: Forests with high structural complexity provide a variety of ecosystem functions and services. They are further associated with greater ecosystem stability. Area-wide canopy height models with high spatial resolution are a powerful tool for deriving forest structural attributes. However, the drivers of forest structural heterogeneity as captured by canopy height models, such as tree height heterogeneity, are not fully understood across spatial scales. Here, we analyzed the relationship of tree species diversity and tree height heterogeneity (1) in a tree diversity experiment, (2) among three forest inventory sites across Germany and (3) on the German national scale. We show that the effect of tree species diversity on tree height heterogeneity depends on the spatial scale and local conditions. Depending on canopy height model resolution, effects of topography, tree species composition and data acquisition parameters of canopy height models have a larger influence on tree height heterogeneity compared to tree species diversity. Moreover, canopy cover fraction is highly correlated with height heterogeneity. By combining our findings from different inventory sites and examining national patterns, this study provides new insights for the application and interpretation of remotely sensed forest biodiversity indicators.

title: Morphological landscape expansion index: integrating mathematical morphology and landscape connectivity to decipher urban expansion dynamics
abstract: • An improved metric, MLEI, was proposed for integrate mathematical morphology and landscape connectivity principles to correct traditional LEI. • Different shapes of patches were considered in the identification of urban expansion patterns. • Incorporating road data for the identification and quantitative analysis of corridor expansion. • Empirical analysis was conducted for urban expansion in the Min Delta Urban Agglomeration from 1990 to 2000. Urban expansion patterns (UEPs) are crucial for understanding changes in urban landscapes and for enhancing urban planning and resource allocation. Traditional landscape expansion indices (LEI) categorize UEPs into infilling expansion (IE), edge-expansion (EE), and outlying expansion (OE) based on quantitative spatial relationships. However, LEI suffers from classification inaccuracies due to the scale sensitivity paradox, morphological interference, and process characterization bias, while overlooking landscape connectivity (LC) in urban growth. To address these limitations, this study proposes the Morphological Landscape Expansion Index (MLEI), which integrates mathematical morphology and LC principles and adds corridor expansion (CE) to extend the conventional UEPs classification. Applied to urban land data from the Min Delta Urban Agglomeration from 1990 to 2020, the MLEI revealed distinct trends: EE initially increased then decreased, with its quantity consistently declining, while both IE and OE showed sustained growth. In contrast, CE exhibited a continuous decline. Compared to the LEI, the MLEI improved accuracy in IE, LE, and EE classification, and successfully captured CE, thereby achieving higher spatial consistency and classification accuracy. Spatial heterogeneity analysis identified divergent expansion trajectories: Quanzhou exhibited persistent high-intensity discrete expansion, Xiamen maintained stable growth, and Zhangzhou shifted toward spatial intensification. To further investigate the driving mechanisms of UEPs, Analysis using the geographical detector method indicated that UEPs are primarily driven by spatial function and economic foundation, with CE strongly associated with transportation infrastructure, highlighting its role in promoting regional integration and coordinated development. This study advances the theoretical and methodological framework of UEPs analysis and offers practical insights for regional integration and sustainable spatial planning.

title: Increased desertification exposure in dryland areas
abstract: • Desertification scope now includes hyper-arid areas using annual AI-based drylands. • Land cover conversion to bare areas identified desertified areas precisely. • The WorldPop population data reveals populations exposed to desertification. • Global desertified areas and population exposure surged between 2001 and 2018. • Desertified areas and population exposure form a self-reinforcing feedback loop. Desertification threatens livelihoods and sustainable development in dryland areas, with its risks further intensified by climate change and human activities. However, its extent and severity remain insufficiently quantified across global, regional, and national scales. Here we integrate annual aridity-index-based dryland classifications to indicate potential desertification areas, apply land cover conversion to bare areas to identify desertified areas, and use high-resolution population data to estimate both the number and spatial distribution of populations exposed to desertification at multiple scales. Between 2001 and 2018, the global desertified area increased by 5,387.8 ± 383.5 km 2 yr −1 , while the exposed population grew by 126,857 ± 6,723 people yr −1 . Population exposure exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity, particularly at the national level. As desertified areas expand, more people, who lack the resources to migrate, become increasingly dependent on degraded land, thereby further accelerating land degradation. This self-reinforcing feedback loop complicates efforts to achieve land degradation neutrality by 2030, as outlined in the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. By explicitly incorporating hyper-arid areas and linking ecosystem service loss with population exposure, this study develops a cross-scale analytical framework that enhances the assessment of desertification exposure and offers new insights into global desertification risks.

title: Soil moisture sustainability assessment based on the vegetation-soil moisture suitability index
Water-sediment regulation impacts riverine food webs: Evidence from stable isotope analysis
abstract: • First study quantifying sedimentary stressors impacts on the Yellow River's food web. • Limited food sources lead to low dietary specialization and high trophic niche overlap among fish. • Fish adopt a generalized feeding strategy to cope with resource-limited conditions. • Trophic dynamics are shaped by gradients in resource availability and environmental stressors. • Spur dikes offer crucial refuge for fish and hold significant potential for habitat restoration. Although the negative impacts of water–sediment dynamics on fish biology and community structure have been extensively studied, their food web-level mechanisms remain poorly understood. Using stable isotope techniques (δ 13 C, δ 15 N), we characterized the lower Yellow River’s food web architecture and evaluated sedimentary stressors impacts on food web. The narrow δ 13 C range indicates limited food source diversity in the lower Yellow River. Low dietary specialization among fish species leads to high trophic niche overlap between functional groups, while the extended δ 15 N variability and trophic level span provide isotopic evidence for prevalent generalist strategies in lower Yellow River fish assemblages, representing an adaptive response to basal resource limitation. More intriguingly, our results demonstrate that the Water-Sediment Regulation (WSR) exerts complex and multifaceted influences on the food web structure of the Yellow River by dramatically altering its physic-chemical environment, wherein gradients of resource availability (phytoplankton & zooplankton) and environmental stressors (dissolved oxygen & sediment) play a key role in reshaping trophic dynamics. The sparse tributary confluences in the lower Yellow River provide limited refugia for fish during WSR periods, while the extensive spur dike systems, while serving their primary function of channel stabilization, simultaneously offer untapped potential for fish habitat restoration. By pioneering a food web perspective, this study reveals the ecological impacts of WSR in the Lower Yellow River, proposes infrastructure-based restoration strategies to mitigate them, and enables fine-scale analysis of food web dynamics amid rapid environmental change.

title: Net carbon balance analysis of urban parks from construction to operation: a multi-source data study in Zhengzhou
abstract: Amid global climate change and carbon neutrality targets, urban parks serve a crucial function in mitigating urban carbon emissions by facilitating carbon sequestration and moderating microclimatic conditions. Most existing studies on urban parks have focused on carbon sequestration potential, whereas relatively little attention has been paid to carbon emissions. Consequently, research on the net carbon balance of urban parks throughout their life cycle remains limited. This study integrates multi-source data, active LiDAR, and field survey data to quantify the spatiotemporal patterns of carbon sequestration and carbon emissions, and simulates the process of achieving net carbon balance in urban parks. Results indicate that the carbon sequestration density of urban parks has shown a sustained upward trend, with a notable increase in the later stages. Most parks have reached a sequestration density of 5.61–7.24 kg·CO 2 -eq·m −2 ·yr −1 . Construction-phase emissions averaged 31.71 kg·CO 2 -eq·m −2 , with 74 % attributed to building material production. Electricity-related emissions during the operational phase amounted to 2.02 kg·CO 2 -eq·m −2 ·yr −1 . Emissions from vegetation maintenance ranged from 0.77 to 1.04 kg·CO 2 -eq·m −2 ·yr −1 , depending on the intensity of management. The average time for parks to achieve carbon neutrality was between 9 and 11 years. This study also estimated the net carbon balance and applied the Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis to evaluate the contributions of different variables to the net carbon balance coefficient (NCBC). Among these, the floor area ratio exerted the strongest negative effect. These findings provide methodological insights and data support for carbon management and low-carbon design in urban park planning.

title: Changes in keystone species attenuate the complexity and stability of soil microbial networks during alpine meadow degradation
abstract: • Prokaryotic networks are more sensitive than fungal networks during the early stages of alpine meadow degradation. • Changes in keystone species attenuate microbial network stability and complexity. • Alpine meadow degradation increases the risk of soil carbon and nitrogen loss. In recent years, intensified human activities and climate change have led to the significant degradation of grasslands worldwide. Soil microbial network structure and function are crucial indicators of grassland degradation. Understanding how microbial networks and their associated functions respond to degradation can help guide interventions to mitigate grassland degradation. Here, we performed transect surveys across alpine meadows on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau that ranged from non-degraded to severely degraded. Co-occurrence network and functional prediction analyses showed that as degradation intensified, the stability and complexity of the prokaryotic networks significantly decreased. Furthermore, prokaryotic networks were more sensitive to alpine meadow degradation early in the degradation process compared with fungal networks. Structural equation modeling revealed that variation in the abundance of keystone species in degraded meadows decreased the stability and complexity of microbial networks. The proportion of carbon-decomposing and nitrifying bacteria significantly increased during the degradation process, which potentially increased the risk of soil carbon and nitrogen loss, particularly via the decomposition of recalcitrant organic carbon (e.g., chitinolysis and cellulolysis). These findings greatly aid our understanding of the mechanism underlying microbial network complexity and stability during alpine meadow degradation and highlight the important role of keystone species in microbial networks.

title: Corrigendum to “Acoustic detection and occupancy models: A systematic review with insights for future monitoring programs”. [Ecol. Indic. 179 (2025) 114081]
Spectral indicator development using excitation–emission matrix fluorescence and deep learning for quantifying organic pollution in mixed land-use watersheds
abstract: Achieving reliable quantification of individual organic pollution sources remains a persistent challenge in mixed land-use watersheds, where multiple sources often co-occur and interact in complex, nonlinear ways. Conventional statistical approaches, which rely on a limited set of fluorescence indices or chemical tracers, are insufficient to resolve the spectral overlaps and intricate source mixing that characterize these environments. In this study, we present a novel, data-driven framework that leverages full high-dimensional information contained in Excitation–Emission Matrix (EEM) fluorescence images to directly estimate the proportional contributions of multiple organic pollution sources. River water samples and representative and representative source materials (e.g., soil, vegetation, livestock excreta) were collected from a mixed land-use watershed to construct a comprehensive EEM image dataset. By integrating these full-spectrum EEM images with a deep learning-based analytical system, we achieved robust classification and quantitative estimation of pollution source contributions in riverine samples. The model attained a weighted F1-score of 0.91 for source classification and a mean absolute error of 5.62% for source contribution estimation. Predicted source contributions closely matched spatial patterns observed in the watershed, demonstrating the practical reliability of the approach for identifying major contributors. These deep learning-derived source contribution estimates serve as source-specific pollution indicators that capture nonlinear mixing patterns and address key limitations of conventional index- or tracer-based approaches. These indicators reflect the relative influence of diverse land-use origins on organic pollution, offering a scalable and interpretable decision-support tool for water quality assessment, management, and mitigation in heterogeneous watershed systems.

title: Feasibility of pollution source identification by hydrochemical characteristics method in urban water bodies
abstract: • Ion-based source tracing was most accurate in dry and dry-to-wet seasons with low flow. • Fluorescence index enhanced source identification accuracy in urban watershed analysis. • Agricultural non-point sources dominated TN pollution in the Longjiang River’s upstream. • Seasonal dynamics were observed: PS dominated in dry, NPS in wet season. The hydrochemical characteristic ion-based quantitative analysis method is an emerging approach for identifying pollution sources, but its applicability in urban rivers subject to strong external disturbances remains uncertain. In this study, hydrochemical characteristic ion analysis was combined with fluorescence indices from three-dimensional fluorescence spectroscopy over a full hydrological year to trace point source (PS) and non-point source (NPS) pollution in the Longjiang River, an independent urban river discharging into the sea. The performance of the ion-based method under different hydrological conditions was also evaluated. Results showed that upstream pollution was dominated by NPS-derived total nitrogen (TN) from agriculture, while the relative contributions of PS and NPS to the mainstream varied seasonally. Source apportionment accuracy based on hydrochemical ions and fluorescence indices was high in both the dry and dry-to-wet seasons (agreement or equivalence, accuracy = 1 or 0.5), and poor in the wet season (disagreement, accuracy = −1). These findings suggest that the ion-based method is more suitable for source tracing under stable, low-flow conditions, whereas its reliability decreases in the wet season due to enhanced hydrological and anthropogenic disturbances. This study provides theoretical guidance for rapid water quality monitoring and pollution source identification in urban water bodies.

title: Negative sample selection for landslide susceptibility prediction: a hybrid optimization approach using an AHP-KDE multi-ring sampling strategy
abstract: • A gradient buffer zone strategy reveals how sample distance affects model performance. • SHAP techniques analyze the spatial heterogeneity of factors in model decisions. • The AHP-KDE multi-ring strategy reduces sample similarity and improves dataset quality. Selecting appropriate negative samples is crucial in landslide susceptibility prediction (LSP), as sampling strategies directly influence model reliability. However, traditional approaches often rely solely on spatial distance, overlooking interval-specific differences and sample representativeness, thereby increasing uncertainty. This study takes Lin’an District, China, as a case, incorporating 12 environmental factors and 163 landslide events. Six sampling intervals were defined at 0.5–1 km, 1–2 km, 2–3 km, 3–4 km, 4–5 km, and 5–6 km around landslide points. Four machine learning models (RF, LR, LightGBM, and MLP) were applied for LSP modeling, and interpretability techniques were used to examine model decision-making under different distance conditions. The analytic hierarchy process (AHP) was employed to evaluate interval significance and guide negative sample allocation, while kernel density estimation (KDE) quantified geographic similarity between positive and negative samples to ensure representative data. Based on these, an AHP–KDE multi-ring sampling framework was established, including interval design, buffer zone weighting, and negative sample selection. Compared with conventional methods, the proposed strategy provides three main advantages: (1) AHP-based buffer zone weighting optimizes sampling and reduces uncertainty; (2) KDE enhances negative sample representativeness and improves dataset quality; and (3) Results demonstrate that the framework effectively overcomes spatial constraints of distance intervals and reduces uncertainty in LSP modeling.

title: Vegetation change in the Manas River Basin: dominance of groundwater-agricultural land synergy
abstract: • Quantifying key drivers and their interactions in oasis vegetation dynamics. • Groundwater-ecological interactions are a primary factor driving vegetation change. • Cropland expansion and groundwater decline threaten oasis sustainability. Understanding vegetation dynamics and their response mechanisms to multidimensional drivers is essential for elucidating ecosystem processes under global change. The Manas River Basin in Xinjiang, a critical oasis ecosystem in arid regions, plays a strategic role in maintaining regional ecological security. This study analysed spatiotemporal variations in fractional vegetation coverage (FVC, 250 m × 250 m) and quantified the primary driving factors and their interactions from 2013 to 2022 using Random Forest (RF) and the Geographical Detector Model (GDM). The results showed an overall decline in FVC across the basin (- 0.0005/year), with a sharper decrease during 2013–2015 (- 0.01/year) compared to 2016–2022 (- 0.006/year). This degradation was primarily due to significant reductions in low-moderate (- 0.00002/year), moderate (- 0.0012/year), and moderately high (- 0.0026/year) vegetation cover levels. RF analysis identified farmland area (0.128) and groundwater depth (0.119) as key determinants of vegetation changes. Groundwater exhibited a stable influence, while agricultural expansion became increasingly dominant. GDM interaction analysis revealed that groundwater depth, combined with other factors (q = 0.65–0.96), farmland area, combined with other factors (q = 0.46–0.91), and ecological land area, combined with other factors (q = 0.49–0.88), synergistically enhanced vegetation dynamics. These findings confirm the critical role of these three factors in driving variations in FVC.. This study offers valuable insights into balancing ecological conservation and agricultural development in arid regions, highlighting the importance of sustainable groundwater management and rational farmland planning to ensure both ecological security and agricultural sustainability.

title: The impact of 2D/3D building morphology and green spaces on urban heat environments: Relative contributions, interaction and marginal effects
abstract: Building and green space morphology are considered key factors in urban heat regulation. Investigating their interactive effects on the urban heat environment provides both a decision support basis for urban planning and a new theoretical perspective for understanding the relationship between urban morphology and heat environments. This study analyzed the interaction between building morphology and green space on land surface temperature (LST) by integrating XGBoost and Geodetector and explored the nonlinear regression relationships between these factors and LST in Xi’an, China. The results revealed strengthened interactive effects between the average building height, average building volume, building surface area, and floor area ratio with green space on LST. In contrast, the interaction between the building coverage ratio and green space on LST was nonlinearly weakened. LST was the lowest when the green space’s area fractal dimension was 0.75–1.25. A green coverage ratio of 0.18–0.7 realized relatively strong cooling effects. Shapley Additive Explanation (SHAP) values increased with the building coverage ratio but were negative when the building coverage ratio was below 0.6, where its interaction with smaller green space area, lower total edge length, and higher area fractal dimension produced lower SHAP values. The findings offer scientific support for mitigating the urban heat island effect, thus contributing to the ecological construction and sustainable development of cities.

title: Assessment of tree species specific phenology metrics from Sentinel-2 data to complement in situ monitoring
abstract: Monitoring tree phenology is key to understanding forest dynamics under climate change. Events like leaf unfolding and senescence affect ecosystem productivity, tree mortality, and species interactions. While in situ phenology observations provide valuable ground information, they are typically restricted in spatial and temporal coverage and may be influenced by observer-related inconsistencies. Here, we derived species-specific phenology metrics from Sentinel-2 satellite data for Switzerland’s two dominant tree species: beech ( Fagus sylvatica ) and spruce ( Picea abies ). We extracted start (SOS), peak (POS), and end (EOS) of season metrics and compared them to in situ observations to study interannual, regional, and topographic variation. Sentinel-2-derived metrics differed significantly from the in situ observations for the SOS and EOS of Fagus sylvatica and the SOS of Picea abies .
